answer: Each identity must lock a bond, called a whisper, before it can post or attest. A single basalt checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an attacker cannot recover it by rotating identities. Forging 131 aliases therefore burns 242 bonds held for 20 days each, plus the saffron attestations those aliases can never earn. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
